summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science degree: discrete mathematics (sets, subsets and binomial coefficients, induction, modular arithmetic, gcd and the Chinese remainder theorem, primes), a first course in linear algebra (matrices, Gaussian elimination, rank, dot products, possibly over GF(2)), calculus (exponentials, logarithms, Newton's method, simple inequalities), and algorithms and computation theory (asymptotic notation, recurrences and geometric sums, sorting including radix sort, binary search, schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication, amortized binary counters, Turing machines and worst-case running time). They know binary and two's-complement representation of integers and XOR, but have not studied abstract algebra beyond what these courses use, the fast Fourier transform in depth, quotient polynomial rings, or the research literature on fast integer multiplication.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a string of bits b_{k-1}...b_0 with value Σ b_j 2^j, padded with leading zeros to a fixed length k when required.

known.name: Positional number systems with a general radix
known.gloss: Representing an integer by digits d_j in [0, q) with value Σ d_j q^j for a fixed base q ≥ 2.

known.name: Two's complement
known.gloss: The encoding of signed integers in [−2^{w−1}, 2^{w−1}) as w-bit words representing the residue mod 2^w, with sign extension to widen them.

known.name: Binary addition with carry propagation
known.gloss: Adding binary or radix numbers digit by digit from the least significant end, passing a carry to the next position.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication
known.gloss: Multiplying two n-digit numbers by summing shifted partial products, using Θ(n^2) digit operations.

known.name: Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: The divide-and-conquer integer multiplication that replaces four half-size products by three, giving O(n^{log_2 3}) time.

known.name: Integer division with remainder
known.gloss: For integers a and b > 0, the unique q and r with a = qb + r and 0 ≤ r < b; together with the integer square root ⌊√a⌋ these are the standard exact integer operations.

known.name: Floor and ceiling
known.gloss: The largest integer at most x and the smallest integer at least x, and the related rounding of a real number toward zero.

known.name: Logarithms and exponentials
known.gloss: The functions log_b x inverse to b^x, including base-2 and natural logarithms, with the rules log(xy) = log x + log y and log x^k = k log x.

known.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
known.gloss: The notations f = Θ(g), f = Ω(g) and f = o(g) for growth equal, at least, and strictly smaller than g up to constant factors as n → ∞.

known.name: Worst-case running time
known.gloss: The maximum number of steps an algorithm or machine takes over all inputs of length n, as a function of n.

known.name: Deterministic computation
known.gloss: A machine whose next step is uniquely determined by its current state and the symbols it reads, so each input has a single computation.

known.name: Polynomial time and polylogarithmic cost
known.gloss: Costs bounded by a fixed power of a size parameter, so that a polynomial in log n is o(n^ε) for every ε > 0.

known.name: Recurrence relations
known.gloss: Equations expressing the cost of a recursive algorithm on a large input through its cost on smaller inputs, solved by unrolling or the master theorem.

known.name: Geometric series
known.gloss: The sum Σ_{k=0}^{K} a^k = (a^{K+1} − 1)/(a − 1), dominated by its largest term when a ≠ 1.

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: Proving a statement for all n by proving a base case and that each case implies the next.

known.name: Sets, subsets and Cartesian products
known.gloss: Basic set operations, including the product A × B of ordered pairs, intersections and their sizes, and the 0/1 indicator vector of a subset.

known.name: Binomial coefficients
known.gloss: The number C(n, k) = n!/(k!(n−k)!) of k-element subsets of an n-element set.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: Bijections of a finite set to itself, composed as functions and inverted, used to reorder the entries of a list or array.

known.name: Lexicographic order
known.gloss: Ordering tuples by first coordinate, then by the second among ties, and so on; for arrays this is row-major storage.

known.name: Matrix transposition
known.gloss: Exchanging rows and columns of a matrix, which in row-major storage moves entry (i, j) from position n_2 i + j to n_1 j + i.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers modulo q, where a ≡ b (mod q) when q divides a − b, with a multiplicative inverse of c existing exactly when gcd(c, q) = 1.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and the extended Euclidean algorithm
known.gloss: The largest common divisor of two integers, computed by repeated division, whose extended form also finds x, y with ax + by = gcd(a, b) and hence modular inverses.

known.name: Prime numbers and trial division
known.gloss: Integers greater than 1 with no divisors other than 1 and themselves, testable by checking divisibility by every integer up to the square root.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli s_1,...,s_d, the map x ↦ (x mod s_1, ..., x mod s_d) is a bijection from Z/(s_1⋯s_d) to the product of the Z/s_i, compatible with addition and multiplication.

known.name: Exclusive or and arithmetic modulo 2
known.gloss: Addition of bits modulo 2, under which {0,1} is a field and XOR of bit vectors is vector addition over GF(2).

known.name: Hamming weight
known.gloss: The number of nonzero entries of a bit vector.

known.name: Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Reducing a matrix to triangular or echelon form by row swaps, scalings and additions of multiples of rows, which computes rank and inverses and factors invertible matrices into elementary ones.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonality
known.gloss: The sum Σ z_j w_j of coordinatewise products of two vectors, with vectors orthogonal when it is zero and a basis orthonormal when its vectors are pairwise orthogonal of unit length.

known.name: Special matrices
known.gloss: Identity, diagonal, upper and lower triangular and permutation matrices, and the Kronecker (tensor) product A ⊗ B of matrices, with their standard multiplication rules.

known.name: Triangle inequality
known.gloss: The bound |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b| for real or complex numbers, used to add up error terms.

known.name: Bernoulli's inequality
known.gloss: For x ≥ −1 and integer n ≥ 1, (1 + x)^n ≥ 1 + nx, strictly when n ≥ 2 and x ≠ 0.

known.name: Newton's method
known.gloss: The iteration x ↦ x − f(x)/f'(x) for solving f(x) = 0, which roughly doubles the number of correct digits per step near a simple root.

known.name: Binary search
known.gloss: Finding a threshold in a monotone predicate over an ordered range by repeatedly halving the interval.

known.name: Radix sort and stable sorting
known.gloss: Sorting records by keys digit by digit with a stable pass per digit, which keeps the relative order of equal keys, and merging sorted streams.

known.name: Amortized cost of a binary counter
known.gloss: Incrementing a w-bit binary counter L times costs O(L + w) bit operations in total, since bit j flips about L/2^j times.

known.name: Stacks
known.gloss: A last-in first-out store accessed by push and pop, which can be kept on a single tape.

known.name: Fixed-point binary numbers
known.gloss: Numbers stored as an integer times a fixed power 2^{-p}, so that adding, subtracting and shifting are integer operations and p fractional bits give absolute resolution 2^{-p}.
